mint-canvas.$description: Mint Canvas — Page background, card surfaces — the signature pastel that makes dark type appear sunlit rather than printed

lime-spark.$description: Lime Spark — Decorative typographic flourishes and SVG scribble overlays — a raw signal-green that contrasts the pastel canvas without warming it

carbon-ink.$description: Carbon Ink — Primary text, borders, icon strokes, button outlines — softer than pure black, sits on mint without vibrating

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Display-type fills at the largest sizes, pure-black SVG fills for the heaviest display specimens

fog.$description: Fog — Muted helper text, inactive borders, disabled controls — the quietest readable neutral on the mint canvas

smoke.$description: Smoke — Input field borders in resting state — darker than fog to signal interactivity without competing with the canvas

bone.$description: Bone — Light surface for elevated UI bits (button hover, inverted controls) — provides a near-white counterpoint when the canvas needs to recede

paper.$description: Paper — Input field interior, pure-white text on dark inverted moments

aurora-gradient.$description: Aurora Gradient — Supporting palette color for small decorative accents when the core palette needs contrast. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

nan-holo-mono.$description: All interface chrome — navigation, labels, buttons, form controls, metadata, keyboard hints. Set uppercase with +0.075em tracking, the letter-spacing is the signature that makes mono read as a deliberate UI system rather than terminal output. The weight range lets it flex from thin nav links to heavy button text without leaving the family.

nan-holo.$description: Prose body and large secondary headlines that need to sit beside display specimens without competing. The 86px weight-300 size is a typographic statement — a humanist counterweight to the blocky display faces above it.

nan-archy-on-extrablack.$description: Hero display headline — the signature specimen face, shown at its native 228px with tight 0.90 leading so the letterforms stack into a near-monolithic mass. This is the typeface the homepage exists to sell.

nan-superx-sans-display-black.$description: Secondary display face — ultra-tight 0.85 leading creates a dense typographic slab, the contrast to Archy's rounded forms. Used in alternate hero rotations.

nan-superx-serif-text-thin-italic.$value: NaN SuperX Serif Text Thin Italic
nan-superx-serif-text-thin-italic.$description: Editorial italic display — the serif counterpoint that proves the practice spans humanist letterforms, not just geometric sans. Thin weight at 216px is a tension device: fragile strokes at monumental size.

nan-holo-gigawide-ultra1.$description: Ultra-condensed display at 336px — the widest single-character scale on the site, used sparingly as a one-word exclamation.

nan-rage-family-zipp-soft-beau-sans-narr.$value: NaN Rage family (Zipp, Soft, Beau, Sans Narrow)
nan-rage-family-zipp-soft-beau-sans-narr.$description: Card specimen headlines in the 'You Might Have Missed' grid — each card shows the family name rendered in that exact family at 86px, making the grid self-documenting.
